A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mimic Score and Grad-Mimic research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original noisy-label classification, DataComp CLIP training and filtering, efficiency, and reference-model robustness results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds aggregation-method, aggregation-data-size, and reference-initialization results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes the top-k binarization condition from m >= tau to m > tau, changing treatment of scores equal to the cutoff. The projection-based Mimic Score, softmax reweighting, and default Snorkel aggregation remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an experimental effect from this boundary change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six image datasets, small/medium DataComp coverage, and 38 downstream tasks. Clean-CIFAR100 subset selection and pretraining-membership prediction already appear in v3. The new aggregation and reference-seed studies reuse existing coverage; future cross-architecture and marketplace applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: v4 adds actual Stage 2 comparisons against majority vote, FlyingSquid, and UWS alongside Snorkel (Tables 7–8). The small-scale Basic Filtering comparison is removed, while its medium-scale comparison remains. Rho-Loss and influence-based comparisons already existed in v3; their appearance in the main text is not a new baseline addition.

E3.justification: Appendix 14 adds aggregation comparisons using 50% label noise and GMM binarization, plus label-model training on random 0.5%, 1%, 5%, and 10% subsets. Existing metrics, optimizers, batch sizes, and training budgets are retained. Revised clean-split/hold-out descriptions conflict with retained full-training-set comparisons, so actual changes to reference-training splits are not established.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands validation of the offline stage: aggregation quality versus majority vote, alternative aggregators, runtime, and data requirements (Appendix 14). Table 15 additionally tests sensitivity to independently initialized reference models. Temperature, layer-depth, reference-corruption, reduced-reference-data, clean-data utilization, and membership analyses were already present in v3.

E5.justification: v4 reports five independent trials and average F1 scores for the aggregation-subsampling experiment. Table 15 explicitly lists five reference-model seeds and performance variances. v3 mentioned differing initialization seeds but did not provide these statistical reports. This does not establish increased repetition of the retained benchmark experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 7–9 and 15 add aggregation accuracy, runtime, subsampling, and reference-seed results. Small-scale standalone-filter results and Stage 2 task-group scores are removed. v4 Table 1 changes DTD/SGD accuracy at 0.6 noise from 44.44 to 41.44, although its appendices retain 44.44. Dataset-quality correlation becomes +0.903 in prose while the retained plot shows -0.903. Headline CLIP results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A and v4 Appendix 9 retain the same mathematical definitions, smoothness and gradient-noise assumptions, three lemmas, theorem, and proofs. Changes are numbering, typography, and placement rather than mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: v4 adds an explicit contribution concerning generalization across design choices and reference-model quality. The central Mimic Score/Grad-Mimic claims and headline reductions of 20.7% in training steps and 4.7 million samples remain. The newly emphasized 2.6-fold computational comparison was already reported in v3 Appendix E.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands applicability and mechanism discussion: an explicit identical-architecture restriction, a cold-start reference-model workaround, and a qualification concerning the clean-data efficiency experiment. It interprets retained degraded-reference results as evidence of useful optimization guidance beyond distillation and adds discussion of consistency across reference models.

D1.justification: v4 adds a plan to release source code upon publication and specifies the 3072-by-768 CLIP weight matrix used in its efficiency explanation. Existing hardware, optimizer, and training-budget disclosures remain. The exact reference-checkpoint link is retained as a hyperlink; the PDFs do not establish an actual code release.

R1.justification: Appendix 17 substantially expands positioning through connections to cross-architecture weight alignment, data-market valuation, and membership inference, including a new distinction from confidence-based membership methods. Additional citation changes include importance resampling and Ultra-FineWeb, and replacing SigLIP with SigLIP2. The original three related-work themes remain.

P1.justification: v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and experimental narrative, organizes experimental arguments around C1–C5 claims, and expands the contribution list. It reorganizes the appendices, moves impact discussion into the main text and membership prediction into the appendix, and adds a substantial future-work discussion.

P2.justification: v4 adds four analysis tables, condenses the main DataComp tables to aggregate scores, and reorganizes classification tables between the main text and appendix. The membership table is relocated, and the existing influence-comparison plot is displayed twice. These are substantial display changes, although most underlying figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The aggregation and reference-seed studies provide useful validation absent from v3, while explicit architectural and cold-start limitations clarify applicability. These yield a limited overall improvement. Benefits are tempered by removed DataComp detail and new reporting inconsistencies, including Appendix 14's blanket F1-above-95 claim despite Table 7 entries of 94.0 and 92.6, the conflicting DTD baseline, and the correlation-sign error.
